data.gender_notes: Zephyrina is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek 'Zephyros', meaning 'west wind'. In Christian tradition, Zephyrina is the name of a saint who is the patroness of those suffering from wind-related ailments. The name Zephyrina carries the meaning “Wind of the west” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Zephyrina usually hope their child will grow to embody wind of the west and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes renewal and change brought by the wind.
data.etymology: Zephyrina belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Wind of the west.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Zephyrina total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_hebrew.name: זפירינה
in_hebrew.meaning: השם זפירינה נגזר מהמילה זפיר, רוח מערבית
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם זפירינה מקורו במילה העברית זפיר, שפירושה רוח מערבית. הוא קשור לנושא הרוחות והאוויר, ויכול לסמל חופש, תנועה ושינוי. השם נושא קונוטציות של קלילות, רעננות והתחדשות.

in_greek.name: Ζεφυρίνα
in_greek.meaning: Το όνομα Ζεφυρίνα προέρχεται από τη λέξη Ζέφυρος, δυτικός άνεμος
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ζεφυρίνα έχει τις ρίζες του στην ελληνική λέξη Ζέφυρος, που σημαίνει δυτικός άνεμος. Ο Ζέφυρος ήταν ο θεός του δυτικού ανέμου στην ελληνική μυθολογία. Το όνομα Ζεφυρίνα μπορεί να συμβολίζει την απαλότητα, την ευκολία και την ανανέωση που φέρνει ο άνεμος.

in_latin.name: Zephyrina
in_latin.meaning: The name Zephyrina derives from Zephyr, a west wind
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Zephyrina originates from the Latinized form of the Greek word Ζέφυρος (Zephyros), meaning west wind. In Roman mythology, Zephyr was the god of the west wind, known for bringing gentle and mild breezes. The name Zephyrina signifies qualities of gentleness, swiftness, and renewal associated with the west wind.

in_english.name: Zephyrina

Historically, the name has been used in various Christian cultures to signify a connection to divine guidance and inspiration.

data.cultural_impact: Zephyrina is a name with a rich cultural history, rooted in Greek mythology. In ancient Greek beliefs, Zephyrus was the name of the god of the west wind. He was depicted as a benevolent and gentle deity, often associated with springtime and bringing soft breezes. This name carries an inherent connection to nature and the wind - an element synonymous with change, aspiration, and renewal.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, Zephyrina is a powerful symbol of protection and healing for those facing challenges related to wind-related ailments. Her name invokes a sense of tranquility in the face of adversity and the promise of renewal. As a patroness, she provides comfort and strength to those in need, reminding us of the healing power of the natural world, and the refuge found in faith.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Zephyrina is a name derived from Zephyrus, the Greek god of the west wind. In Christian tradition, she is a symbol of gentle refreshment and renewal, bringing the spirit of change and new beginnings. Her name invokes the image of a soft breeze carrying the scent of spring, signifying hope and transformation.

historical_references.reference: Zephyrine was an ancient Roman goddess of the west winds, identified with the Greek god Zephyros. She was worshipped at the Temple of Zephyrus in Rome, which was a popular pilgrimage site for Christians during the 4th-5th centuries AD. The site was later converted into a Christian basilica dedicated to Saint Zephyrina, possibly a martyr from Sicily.

According to the Golden Legend, Zephyrina was a Christian virgin and martyr who was persecuted during the reign of Nero in Rome (c. AD 64). She was said to have miraculously cured a sick man by carrying him to a spring to drink from it. The man was so moved by her kindness that he revealed her as a Christian to the authorities, leading to her arrest, trial, and eventual martyrdom.
